data.name: Antinarkomania
data.detailed_description:
Anti-drug computer game for schoolchildren. “Antinarkomania” belongs to the genre of arcades with elements of the puzzle genre, which implies both high dynamics of the game and the need to think about the constantly arising complex situations and carefully plan their actions for their resolution. The game has an interesting and relevant story, extraordinary gameplay, aimed at creating the maximum dynamics of what is happening, and the development of imaginative thinking of the player, is fully dedicated to the theme of the fight against drugs and the promotion of a healthy lifestyle, in which there is no place for drugs.

In a happy drug-free country Antinarkomania everything was wonderful: adults went to work, children went to school, and toddlers played in the yards. But then unhappy people began to appear in the country, people who couldn't enjoy life or work normally. The authorities suspected something was wrong and brought in a team of renowned detectives and anti-drug traffickers to investigate.

The mafia is not slumbering! The insidious drug is spreading across the country and ruining the lives of millions of citizens. The task of Federal Drug Control Service employees - Inspector, Schoolgirl and Schoolboy - is to eliminate this system and each of its participants. On their way will stand many obstacles and evil bandits and only you can prevent them!

  • Control three unique heroes — the Schoolboy, the Schoolgirl, and the Inspector, each with their own special abilities.

  • Solve exciting puzzles by combining the skills of your characters.

  • Feel the arcade action: hand-to-hand combat, yo-yo throwing, shooting, and a skateboard-shield!

  • Play as a team — protect your allies to overcome the most dangerous challenges.

  • Immerse yourself in the atmosphere of the Moscow metro, filled with traps, mutants, and sinister secrets.

  • Face the evil doctor and the mafia boss — crush their treacherous plans!

  • Every mission is a new test: speed, wit, and tactics decide everything.

  • Classic gameplay inspired by The Lost Vikings — for fans of clever arcade adventures.

  • The Steam edition contains all levels, including 3 additional levels released later.

  • And most importantly — this is not just a game for fun, but also with a mission: friendship, courage, and life without drugs!

reviews.review:
Antinarkomania is one of those unusual games whose concept is almost as interesting as the actual experience of playing it. Developed by PIPE Studio and published by Strategy First, it combines an anti-drug educational message with platforming, puzzle solving, combat, and character switching. Originally created during the mid-2000s, it carries many characteristics of PC games from that period, including straightforward mechanics, modest visuals, and a willingness to experiment with several gameplay styles rather than focusing entirely on one.

The story takes place in a society suffering from a growing drug problem. As more people become affected, an investigation begins to uncover the organization responsible for distributing the substances. The adventure eventually turns into a battle against criminals and other increasingly strange threats. Instead of approaching the subject realistically, the game presents everything through a colorful, exaggerated adventure involving dangerous locations, mutants, villains, traps, and an evil doctor. This cartoon-like direction makes the serious underlying theme considerably less oppressive, although the educational message remains extremely direct.

At the center of the campaign are three playable characters: the Inspector, the Schoolboy, and the Schoolgirl. Each possesses different abilities, and understanding how their skills complement one another is essential to progression. Players frequently need to switch between characters to overcome obstacles or solve environmental puzzles. This creates a teamwork-oriented structure in which the heroes are more valuable together than individually. Certain situations may appear impossible until the correct character is brought into position, giving the game a satisfying problem-solving component.

Puzzle solving is mixed with more active sequences involving platforming and combat. Players encounter enemies and hazards while making use of unconventional equipment and abilities. The inclusion of yo-yo attacks and a skateboard that can serve defensive purposes contributes to the deliberately playful tone. Protecting the entire group also matters because individual characters can be required for specific challenges later in a stage. This encourages a degree of tactical thinking beyond simply defeating everything standing in the way.

The variety of challenges prevents the experience from becoming purely a puzzle platformer. Some sections emphasize careful movement and observation, while others depend more heavily on speed, combat, or determining the proper sequence in which the characters should act. Locations such as the Moscow metro give the adventure a distinctive atmosphere, especially once ordinary surroundings begin filling with exaggerated enemies and hazards. The game is rarely sophisticated in its execution, but it continually introduces enough different situations to keep its basic formula moving.

Its educational purpose is much less subtle. Antinarkomania was clearly designed to promote a drug-free lifestyle, and the narrative presents its message through an uncomplicated struggle between the protagonists and those responsible for spreading drugs. Friendship, teamwork, courage, and healthy living are positioned as positive values. Players expecting complicated discussions about addiction or its social causes will not find them here. The game instead resembles an interactive public-awareness campaign translated into an arcade adventure, making its historical and educational context important when judging its unusual storytelling.

Age is arguably its largest weakness. The graphics, animations, controls, interface, and general presentation reflect technology and design conventions from an earlier generation of PC gaming. The cartoon aesthetic gives the environments and characters some personality, but it cannot completely disguise the technical limitations. Players accustomed to modern platformers may find movement and interaction comparatively stiff. At the same time, those interested in obscure older PC titles may actually find these qualities part of its charm.

The Steam release benefits from containing the complete selection of levels along with three additional stages that were introduced later, making it a more comprehensive edition of the original experience. Its relatively small technical footprint also reflects how lightweight the game is by modern standards. Rather than demanding powerful hardware, its greater challenge on contemporary systems comes from the fact that it was designed around much older PC technology.

Steam Deck compatibility should be regarded as Unverified unless Valve provides an official compatibility rating for the title. Given the game's age and Windows-oriented design, players should not assume flawless handheld operation. It may potentially run through SteamOS and Proton, but controls, resolution behavior, video playback, or other legacy compatibility issues could require manual adjustments. Anyone specifically planning to play it on Steam Deck should therefore approach it as an experimental experience rather than a confirmed plug-and-play title.

Antinarkomania ultimately succeeds more as an unusual gaming curiosity than as a highly polished arcade adventure. Its character-switching mechanics provide genuine puzzle potential, while the combination of teamwork, platforming, combat, and environmental challenges gives the campaign more variety than its educational origins might suggest. The heavy-handed message and dated production values limit its broader appeal, but there is something memorable about a game that combines an anti-drug campaign with schoolchildren, investigators, mutants, mafia villains, skateboards, yo-yos, and puzzle-platforming mechanics. As an unconventional piece of older PC gaming history, it has enough personality to be worth experiencing for players who appreciate obscure and experimental titles.

Rating: 6/10
